findings.text: follow-on: logs/head-arm.log is listed as a base-arm log but its header reads revision 488bb49925a0f21d56b44b44135666e81a7bd9f1 and its summary is '26 passed in 128.20s', i.e. the head result with the fix present (uncommitted) rather than the base result. The manifest's tests field therefore declares a base arm ('1 failed, 25 passed at 488bb4992') that no listed log supports, and a reader computing added failures from the run's own logs would see zero failures at both arms. The base behaviour is evidenced only by logs/negative-control.log (fixture reverted at bb63301f8, 1 failed EXIT=1); I reproduced the true base arm independently (1 failed/25 passed EXIT=1) so the substantive claim holds and only the log labelling is wrong.

follow-on: _dead_pid() returns a pid the fixture has just reaped but does not pin a pid_start_time, so the test's determinism rests on the kernel not reusing that pid before _worker_liveness probes it; a reuse in that window would read the worker as alive and flake the test. Negligible in practice, but it is the one non-deterministic input in the fixture and a future reader changing the hold's pid handling should know the fixture depends on it.

item_verdicts.diff: read bb63301f8 against base 488bb4992; one commit, one file, +12/-0, tests only. The diff adds imports (socket, subprocess, sys), a _dead_pid() helper, and two fixture keys (pid, launcher_host). No assertion in the file changed, so the same assertions that were red at base are green at head.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node's measure is that the fixture's change makes the gate green at head and red at base with the fixture reverted. Reproduced: head 26 passed EXIT=0, base 1 failed/25 passed EXIT=1, and the negative control at head-reverted fails the same id. All three agree.
item_verdicts.evidence: verified against the reviewed run's own logs (head-arm-committed.log = 26 passed EXIT=0 at bb63301f8; negative-control.log = 1 failed EXIT=1 at bb63301f8-reverted) and re-measured independently in scratch trees ($TMPDIR/rev/base and /rev/head): base 1 failed/25 passed EXIT=1, head 26 passed EXIT=0, added failures 0.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to model a prior run whose worker has exited so same-task resolution reads the session its stream names through the member hold. The fixture now records a reaped pid and this host - the exact two fields claims._worker_liveness (claims.py:231-267) reads to answer False - and the same-task test passes at head and fails at base with the hold's withholding reason.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, base 488bb4992 to head bb63301f8, one commit, changed_paths = the one test file, negative_control_log present and red (1 failed EXIT=1). baseline_suite and after_suite are null, and test_logs lists a log (head-arm.log) whose header names the base revision but whose summary is the head result.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the one changed file tests/test_dispatch_reads_the_resolved_session.py lies inside the node's declared grant; the declared fragment and figure paths are unwritten, which is correct for a fixture-only change.

justifications.durability: the change is a genuine regression guard: the fixture now exercises the hold through the real seam, red at base with the withholding reason and green at head, and the negative control (fixture reverted at head) re-reddens the same id, so a future reader that reverted to keying on the raw field would be caught. The fixture still isolates its state under a tmp RECKON_HOME. Docked slightly because _dead_pid() relies on the kernel not reusing the reaped pid before the probe, which is a theoretical flake rather than a driven guarantee.
justifications.evidence: the arms reproduce under my own run: base 1 failed/25 passed EXIT=1 (logs/reviewer-base-gate.log) and head 26 passed EXIT=0 (logs/reviewer-head-gate.log), on the identical four-file gate, so added_failure_count is 0. Docked because the reviewed run's own log chain cannot produce that delta: logs/head-arm.log is labelled revision 488bb4992 (base) yet records 26 passed - the head result, run with the fix in the tree but uncommitted - so the manifest's declared base arm ('1 failed, 25 passed at 488bb4992') is not evidenced by the log it lists, and the base behaviour is shown only by logs/negative-control.log (fixture reverted at bb63301f8, 1 failed EXIT=1). The manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite are null (the run was not armed), so a reader deriving the added-failure figure from the run's declared suite fields gets nothing; I reproduced the base arm myself, which is why the figure is trustworthy even though the run's logs are not.
justifications.fit: the fix is minimal and named by mechanism - a fixture field addition plus a one-line helper - using only the stdlib (socket, subprocess, sys); the docstring states why a reaped pid reads as gone. It models the real shape of a finished run's pointer (a worker pid that is now dead, stamped with the host that launched it), which is what the hold actually reads, so it adds no product logic and no duplicated resolution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's deliverable is met and independently reproduced: the run_with_stream fixture now records the two fields claims._worker_liveness reads to prove a worker gone - pid = a process spawned and reaped inside the fixture (probe -> gone) and launcher_host = socket.gethostname() (this host) - so dispatch._task_session_resolution reads the prior run's session from its stream instead of withholding it. I reproduced both arms in scratch trees: base 488bb4992 = 1 failed (test_same_task_dispatch_reuses_session_named_only_by_prior_stream) / 25 passed EXIT=1, head bb63301f8 = 26 passed EXIT=0. The base failure carries the exact withholding reason the manifest quotes ('it records no worker process yet, and a pointer is written before its worker is spawned'), so the fix targets the hold and nothing else.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff writes exactly one path, tests/test_dispatch_reads_the_resolved_session.py (+12 lines, insertions only), which is within the node's grant; no product source changed and no shared plan, sprint or index state was touched. The node declares a fragment and a figure path in its grant and correctly writes neither - the change is a fixture edit too small to carry a figure, and the dispatch names none.
